title: Practical 1
description: Simulation of Random Experiments (Coin Toss & Dice Roll)

items.content: Question 1: Coin Toss Simulation A fair coin is tossed 100 times. Simulate 100 coin tosses using Python. Count the number of Heads and Tails. Calculate the empirical probability of obtaining a Head. Calculate the empirical probability of obtaining a Tail. Compare the empirical probabilities with the theoretical probabilities: P(H)=0.5,P(T)=0.5

items.code:
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

# Simulate 100 coin tosses
tosses = np.random.choice(['Head', 'Tail'], size=100)

# Count Heads and Tails
heads = np.sum(tosses == 'Head')
tails = np.sum(tosses == 'Tail')

# Calculate empirical probabilities
prob_heads = heads / len(tosses)
prob_tails = tails / len(tosses)

# Print results
print('Heads:', heads)
print('Tails:', tails)

# Print probabilities
print('Probability of Heads:', prob_heads)
print('Probability of Tails:', prob_tails)

# Print theoretical probabilities
print('Theoretical probability of Head:', 0.5)
print('Theoretical probability of Tail:', 0.5)

items.content: Repeat the coin-toss experiment for: n=10,100,1000,10000,100000Calculate the empirical probability of Heads for each sample size. Plot the empirical probability of Heads against the number of tosses. Add a reference line representing the theoretical probability (P(H)=0.5).

items.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Simulate coin tosses
sample_size = [10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000]
probability = []

for n in sample_size:
    np.random.seed(42)
    tosses = np.random.choice(['Head', 'Tail'], size=n)

    heads = np.sum(tosses == 'Head')
    prob = heads / n
    probability.append(prob)

    print("Number of tosses:", n)
    print("Empirical probability of Head:", prob)
    print()

# Plot the graph
plt.plot(sample_size, probability, marker='o')

# Theoretical probability
plt.axhline(y=0.5, linestyle='--', label='Theoretical P(H) = 0.5')

plt.xlabel("Number of Tosses")
plt.ylabel("Empirical Probability of Heads")
plt.title("Empirical Probability of Heads vs Number of Tosses")
plt.xscale('log')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

items.content: Question 2: Dice Roll Simulation A fair six-sided die is rolled 10,000 times. Let X denote the outcome of a roll. Estimate the following probabilities: 1. P(X=6) 2. P(X is even) 3. P(X>4) 4. P(X≤3) Compare the empirical probabilities with their theoretical probabilities. Are the empirical and theoretical probabilities exactly equal? Why or why not?

items.code:
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

# Simulate 10000 dice rolls
rolls = np.random.randint(1, 7, size=10000)

# Calculate the empirical probabilities
p_6 = np.mean(rolls == 6)
p_even = np.mean(rolls % 2 == 0)
p_greater_4 = np.mean(rolls > 4)
p_less_equal_3 = np.mean(rolls <= 3)

# Print the results
print("P(X = 6):", p_6)
print("P(X is even):", p_even)
print("P(X > 4):", p_greater_4)
print("P(X <= 3):", p_less_equal_3)

items.content: NO, the theoretical and empirical probabilities are not exactly same they differ as the trial perform is low so the probabilities slightly differ. title: Practical 2
description: Probability Distributions & Parameter Estimation (Normal, Poisson, Exponential, Noise Analysis)

items.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

items.content:
Q1) A data analyst wants to model the distribution of examination scores.

1. Generate 500 normally distributed observations with mean 70 and standard deviation 10.
2. Plot a histogram of the observations.
3. Fit a Normal distribution to the data.
4. Overlay the fitted Normal PDF on the histogram.
5. Report the estimated mean and standard deviation.

items.code:
np.random.seed(42)
data = np.random.normal(loc=70, scale=10,size=500)

#fit normal distribution
mu, sigma = stats.norm.fit(data)

#histogram
plt.hist(data, bins=20, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='g')

#fitted pdf
x = np.linspace(data.min(), data.max(), 300)
pdf = stats.norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)
plt.plot(x, pdf, linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel("Examination Score")
plt.ylabel("Probability Density")
plt.title("Normal Distribution: Observed Data and Fitted PDF")
plt.show()

print("Estimated Mean:", mu)
print("Estimated Standard Deviation:",sigma)

items.content:
Q2) A website receives a certain number of customer support requests per minute. Assume that the number of requests can be modelled using a Poisson distribution.

1. Generate 500 observations assuming an average of 4 requests per minute.
2. Plot the frequency distribution.
3. Estimate the Poisson parameter λ
4. Overlay the fitted Poisson probabilities.
5. Compare the observed and fitted distributions.

items.code:
np.random.seed(42)
data=np.random.poisson(lam=4, size=500)

#estimated lambda
lambda_hat = np.mean(data)

#observed values
values, counts = np.unique(data, return_counts=True)
observed_prob = counts/ len(data)

#fitted poisson probabilities
fitted_prob = stats.poisson.pmf(values, lambda_hat)

#plot
plt.bar(values, observed_prob, alpha=0.6, label="Observed")
plt.plot(values, fitted_prob,'o-',linewidth=2, alpha=0.6, label="Fitted")

plt.xlabel("Number of Requests per Minute")
plt.ylabel("Probability")
plt.title("Poisson Distribution: Observed vs. Fitted")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

print("Estimated Lambda:", lambda_hat)

Q7. Calculate the Probability of a Hidden-State and Observation Sequence
Consider the following hidden-state sequence:
Noun → Verb
and the observed sequence:
dogs → bark
Calculate the joint probability of this state-observation sequence using:

P(Noun)×P(dogs|Noun)×P(Verb|Noun)×P(bark|Verb)

Write Python code to calculate the probability.

# Hidden-state sequence

state_2 = "Verb"

observation_1 = "dogs"
observation_2 = "barks"

state_2_index = states.index(state_2)

observation_2_index = observation.index(observation_2)

]

    state_2_index
]

]

print("P(bark | Verb) =", p4)

title: Practical 8
description: PageRank Algorithm & Random Walk Simulation (Directed Graphs)

items.code:
import networkx as nx
import random
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from collections import Counter


#create directed graph
G = nx.DiGraph()
edges=[
    ("A","B"),
    ("A","C"),
    ("B","C"),
    ("B","D"),
    ("C","A"),
    ("C","D"),
    ("D","A"),
    ("D","C")
]

G.add_edges_from(edges)

#VISUALIZE THE NETWORK
nx.draw(G, with_labels=True, node_size=2000,arrows=True)
plt.title("Directed Webpage Network")
plt.show()

#Random Walk
current = 'A'
walk = [current]
random.seed(42)

for _ in range(20):
  neighbours = list(G.successors(current))
  current = random.choice(neighbours)
  walk.append(current)
print("Random Walk:", walk)

#count visits
visit_counts = Counter(walk)
print("Visit Counts:", visit_counts)

for page in G.nodes():
  print(page,":",visit_counts[page])

#PageRank
pagerank = nx.pagerank(G)
print("PageRank:", pagerank)

for page, score in sorted(pagerank.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
  print(page,":",round(score,4))

items.content: **the highest pagerank means the higher probability of user staying on that page at the end**
